title: Lifting Micro-Update Models from RTL for Formal Security Analysis
problem: Handwriting accurate abstract formal models of hardware is tedious and error-prone, and full hardware verification does not scale for checking security properties against microarchitectural execution attacks.
motivation: Hardware execution attacks exploiting microarchitectural interactions leak secret data and must be prevented through scalable formal verification with strong security guarantees.
method: Instead of manually writing formal models describing how hardware behaves, this approach automatically extracts simplified models from the RTL specification (a detailed register-level description of the hardware). The extraction process is designed so that any security property proven in the simplified model is guaranteed to hold in the actual hardware. This enables practical checking for microarchitectural vulnerabilities—attacks exploiting low-level details of CPU execution—without the complexity of verifying full hardware.
key_novelty: Automatically extracting formal security models directly from hardware RTL specifications, eliminating manual model construction.
contributions: Automated model lifting technique from RTL for formal security analysis
Sound abstraction approach preserving security property verification
Scalability improvement over full hardware verification
Reduction of manual effort in formal model creation
primary_theme: Automated formal model generation from hardware RTL for security analysis
